title: Article Extraction Template v2.0
description: JSON Schema for article extraction output. Defines the complete structure of findings extracted from scientific articles using Article Eater, including stimulus descriptions, theory commitments, mechanism chains, and instrument tracking.

doi.description: Digital Object Identifier of the article

article_type.description: Classification of article type based on methodology and scope

quality_action.description: Quality control action taken on this extraction batch

quality_score.description: Overall extraction quality score [0, 1]. Computed as median of finding quality scores.

n_findings.description: Number of findings extracted from this article

extracted_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp when extraction was performed

usd.description: Estimated USD cost of API call

detected_article_type.description: Article type as detected by the model (may differ from article_type if user override)

detected_family.description: Article family as detected by the model

classification_confidence.description: Model confidence in article type/family classification

classification_signals.description: Signals that drove article classification (e.g., 'METHODS section present', 'empirical n reported')

findings.description: Array of extracted findings from the article

overall_theory_links.description: High-level theory commitments cited throughout the article

limitations.description: Limitations acknowledged by the authors or inferred from the paper

minimum_safe_summary.description: A conservative summary of the paper's main claims, suitable for downstream systems with low tolerance for hallucination

extraction_metadata.description: Metadata tracking extraction provenance, model details, and inter-rater reliability

extraction_confidence.description: Model's self-assessed confidence in the extraction (0=very uncertain, 1=very confident)

dual_extraction.description: Whether this article was extracted twice by independent extractors for reliability assessment

inter_extraction_agreement.description: Inter-rater reliability / agreement score if dual_extraction=true (e.g., Fleiss' kappa, Cronbach's alpha)

citation_count.description: Citation count (if available from external database)

references.description: Number of references cited in the paper

cited_by.description: Number of papers citing this paper (if available)

antecedent.description: Independent variable, stimulus, or environmental condition. Must be specific and operationalized.

consequent.description: Dependent variable or outcome measured. Describes the measured response, not the condition.

direction.description: Effect direction: increase/decrease in consequent, no_effect, or mixed results across conditions

claim_type.description: Classification of claim: empirical (with statistics), theoretical, or narrative

p_value.description: P-value from statistical test. Numeric [0,1] preferred; may be string like '< 0.001' if reported that way.

effect_size.description: Magnitude of effect (e.g., Cohen's d, correlation r, odds ratio). Sign should match direction.

effect_size_type.description: Name of the effect size statistic used

sample_size.description: Number of participants or observations in the study

sample_size_source.description: Whether sample_size was directly reported, inferred from text, or estimated from context

confidence_interval.description: 95% confidence interval as [lower, upper]. Both values must be numeric.

theory_links.description: Theories or frameworks invoked to explain or contextualize this finding

template_ids.description: IDs of stimulus templates this finding applies to (links to stimulus_template registry)

mechanism.description: Proposed mechanism explaining the relationship between antecedent and consequent

moderators_reported.description: Variables that moderate the antecedent-consequent relationship

provenance_depth.description: How directly the extraction comes from the paper

quote.description: Direct quote from the paper supporting this finding

stimulus_description.description: Detailed description of the stimulus or environmental manipulation used in this finding

stimulus_images.description: Images or visualizations of the stimulus

theory_commitments.description: How this finding relates to broader theories (tests, extends, contradicts, assumes, proposes)

mechanism_chain.description: Step-by-step mechanism linking antecedent to consequent. Conditionally required: required for 'causal' and 'mechanistic' claim_types in empirical papers; expected but not required for theoretical papers if central_proposition is present; optional for qualitative and narrative claims.

mechanism_expectation.description: Expectation level for mechanism_chain based on claim_type and article context

molecule_ids.description: Links to rasa_attractors.json entries this finding relates to (semantic/causal molecules)

instruments_used.description: Measurement instruments or scales used in this finding

StimulusDescription.description: Comprehensive description of a stimulus or experimental manipulation

primary_type.description: Primary sensory modality of the stimulus

components.description: Individual components or elements of the stimulus

equivalence_class_id.description: ID linking to other equivalent or comparable stimuli across papers

delivery_method.description: How the stimulus was presented to participants

duration_seconds.description: Duration of stimulus presentation in seconds (null if not applicable)

stimulus_temporal.description: Temporal properties of the stimulus exposure (critical moderators in environmental psychology)

exposure_frequency.description: Pattern of exposure: single/discrete, continuous, or intermittent

exposure_prior_familiarity.description: Participant familiarity with stimulus prior to study (0=novel, 1=very familiar)

habituation_control.description: Whether habituation/adaptation was controlled in the study design

name.description: Name or description of the component (e.g., 'window size', 'color temperature', 'noise level')

category.description: Category or domain of the component

essential.description: Whether this component is essential to the stimulus definition (vs. incidental)

StimulusImage.description: Reference to an image documenting the stimulus

description.description: What the image shows (e.g., 'VR scene rendered at 1920x1080')

theory_name.description: Name of the theory or framework (e.g., 'Cognitive Load Theory', 'Stress-Reduction Theory')

framework_id.description: Identifier linking to a theory registry or ontology

commitment_type.description: How this finding relates to the theory: tests (empirically evaluates), extends (builds on), contradicts (refutes), assumes (takes as given), proposes (introduces novel claim)

specific_claim.description: The specific claim or prediction from the theory being engaged with

step.description: Sequential step number in the causal chain (must be consecutive integers starting at 1)

from_construct.description: Starting construct or variable (antecedent of this step)

to_construct.description: Ending construct or variable (consequent of this step)

mechanism_type.description: Type of mechanism connecting the constructs

evidence_strength.description: Strength of evidence for this mechanism step: direct (explicitly tested), indirect (inferred from correlates), theoretical (proposed but not tested), assumed (taken as given)

evidence_reference.description: Citation or source supporting this mechanism step

SuccessConditions.description: Criteria for evaluating whether this finding is usable/credible. Separates data-tier requirements (minimum fields and quality) from epistemic-tier expectations (theory and mechanism grounding).

required_fields.description: Fields that must be non-null for this finding to pass data validation (e.g., ['antecedent', 'consequent', 'direction'])

min_quality_score.description: Minimum acceptable quality score (varies by article_family)

theory_link_expected.description: Whether this finding should link to at least one theory (varies by claim_type: true for causal/mechanistic, false for narrative)

mechanism_expected.description: Whether a mechanism explanation is expected (true for causal, false for qualitative_theme)

min_findings.description: Minimum number of replications or supporting findings needed for robust claim

name.description: Name of the measurement instrument or scale (e.g., 'State-Trait Anxiety Inventory', 'NASA-TLX'). Must not be vague.

construct_measured.description: What psychological/physiological construct the instrument measures

n_items.description: Number of items if it's a scale
